name: Transaction / ledger row
purpose: A STATEMENT LINE IN A LEDGER: an ordered sequence of settled and pending entries with a RUNNING BALANCE, column headers, day grouping and a closing total. Its question is 'what was the balance after this?', which is a relationship between rows and therefore a table. PROPOSED #209 (itinerary row 91, slug transaction-row, P2) — NOT GATED, NOT RULED. Fintech semantics are Dave's (the Kpi-tile precedent, s182-D2).

It is not a gap … I built no transaction row.'). Its evidence is real and was RE-PROBED at #209, not trusted: list-items.meta.json build.$status = 'PROMOTED 2026-06-22 (Dave) — TRANSACTION row brought to the Tabs-bar standard'; build.scope = 'Transaction row only (the ★ payments-journey row)'; build.prototypeGrade = '9.0/9 (2026-06-22)'; List-items.reference.html <title> = 'List items — Transaction row (reference implementation, gated)'. THE TAPPABLE TRANSACTION ROW IS GATED AND PROMOTED AND IS NOT RE-DRAWN ANYWHERE IN THIS COMPONENT. The #209 brief re-listed row 91 as a build because the itinerary re-probe reads by SLUG, which is the exact mechanism defect Lane N named. This lane did not resolve that by building what Lane N stopped: it built the one form the adjudication does not cover — the LEDGER, with a running balance. ⬛ IF DAVE RULES THAT THE PRODUCT'S STATEMENT IS A LIST AND NOT A LEDGER, THIS COMPONENT SHOULD NOT EXIST and row 91 collapses into List-items exactly as Lane N said. That is a live outcome; deleting this pair of files costs nothing, because nothing registers them.

props.name: entries
props.$note: Ordered, newest first. Each entry: payee, reference line, one money value, and the balance AFTER it. Order is meaning here — a running balance cannot be reordered client-side without becoming false.

props.name: moneyColumns
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P1). 'two' = separate Money out / Money in columns, the UK statement convention, which carries the sign STRUCTURALLY. 'signed' = one Amount column carrying a U+2212. Both forms are DRAWN in the reference so Dave chooses by eye rather than from prose. Whichever he picks, the figure is monochrome.

props.name: runningBalance
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P3). This is the DISCRIMINATOR: with it false, the component IS a List-items transaction list and should be one. A pending entry shows an em dash, not a number, because the balance does not exist until it settles.

props.name: groupBy
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P5). Rendered as <th scope="rowgroup"> day headings. The alternative is a date column on every row — denser, equally buildable.

props.name: status
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P4). Rendered as a Status-indicator RAG-tint chip ALWAYS CARRYING ITS WORD; 'settled' draws no chip at all, because 400 green chips on a statement is noise. Which status maps to which chip tint is a SEMANTIC binding and is DAVE'S.

props.name: referenceLine
props.$note: PROPOSED, NOT RULED (P6). 'Card ending 4821 · Faster Payment'. Whether the method, the reference, the merchant category or none of them belongs on line 2 is unruled. It is the first thing to drop below 400c.

props.name: closingBalance
props.$note: Rendered in a real <tfoot> so assistive technology announces it as a total rather than as another row.

variants.name: two-column
variants.use: The default. Money out / Money in / Balance — the sign is carried by the COLUMN, a non-colour channel a signed column does not have.

variants.name: signed
variants.use: One Amount column with a U+2212, and the running balance moved onto the reference line. What a phone width wants.

variants.name: pending
variants.use: An entry that has not settled: a Pending chip and an em dash where the balance will be.

variants.name: reversed
variants.use: A refund or reversal: the money returns in the Money in column and the chip says so.

tokens.hover: tertiary/background/hover — row hover, the day-group band and the tfoot band
tokens.text: text/default — every figure, every payee, and the closing balance
tokens.muted: text/secondary — column heads, day headings, the reference line
tokens.divider: divider/border/section — the 1px rules between rows and under the heads
tokens.status: rag/warning + rag/warning-tint (pending) | rag/information + rag/information-tint (reversed) | rag/success + rag/success-tint (declared, unused by the drawn specimens)
tokens.focus: focus/ring — the scroll region's focus outline
tokens.radius: border-radius/surface (the table shell) + border-radius/indicator (the chip). 0 in Mono and Legacy; Console forks surface through the cascade.
tokens.$note: NO NEW TOKEN IS WANTED OR MINTED. Every value here already exists and is already bound by a gated component. ⛔ AND NO MONETARY COLOUR TOKEN IS BOUND AT ALL — see $moneyColour.

$moneyColour: ⛔ THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS FILE. A debit/credit ledger is the single most likely place in this system for a red/green money binding to get improvised. NONE IS. Every figure in every column is text/default, monochrome; the sign is carried by U+2212 and by the COLUMN the figure sits in. The system DOES own coloured monetary seats — Amount-display's sign=positive → rag.success-ink and sign=negative → rag.error-ink, MONO ONLY (s155-D1 / s158-D2 / s158-D3) — and they are DELIBERATELY NOT BOUND HERE. Whether a ledger credit is that seat is a SEMANTIC binding and is DAVE'S (question Q1 in the receipt). Binding it would have been ruling on his behalf.

motion.hover: Row background to tertiary/background/hover over the inherited 140ms ease.

responsive.rule: Container-query at 400c: cell padding tightens to 12px and the reference line drops before the payee does (P6). The two money FORMS are two tables, not a breakpoint switch — see knownFindings, that was a corrected defect. The table sits in a labelled role="region" with tabindex="0" so a genuinely narrow viewport can still reach the right-hand columns from the keyboard (2.1.1).

mustNotNeighbour: A List-items transaction list showing the SAME entries (two components claiming to be the same statement)

accessibility.role: A real <table> with <caption>, scoped column heads, <th scope="rowgroup"> day headings and a <tfoot> total. The relation between a row's amount and the row above it is what the table encodes and what a list of buttons cannot (1.3.1).
accessibility.name: The caption names the account and the period. The scroll region carries its own aria-label.
accessibility.scrollRegion: The table sits in role="region" tabindex="0" — THE ONLY FOCUSABLE THING IN THE COMPONENT — because a horizontally scrollable region must be keyboard reachable (2.1.1) and must show focus (2.4.7). Added after _validate_snippets.py caught 'no :focus-visible rule'.
accessibility.pendingBalance: The em dash where a pending balance would be carries an aria-label ('No balance yet, this payment has not settled') so it is not announced as a bare dash.
accessibility.notColourAlone: No meaning anywhere rests on hue. Status carries its WORD in the chip; the sign carries a U+2212 and its column. Remove all colour and the component still says everything it means (1.4.1).
accessibility.hitArea: The component contains NO CONTROL, so the 44px minimum has no seat here. Declared rather than assumed. The one focusable element is the scroll region, which is not a control.
accessibility.keyboard: Tab reaches the scroll region and arrow keys scroll it. No row is individually focusable — a 400-line statement must not be 400 tab stops.

antiPatterns: ⛔ MAKING EACH LEDGER ROW INDIVIDUALLY TAPPABLE. That is a List-items transaction row wearing a table: it exists, it is gated, it is Dave-promoted at 9.0/9, and this component must not duplicate it. If the product needs tappable rows, use List-items type="transaction".
⛔ DROPPING THE RUNNING BALANCE AND KEEPING THE TABLE. Without the running balance there is no cross-row relation, and the component IS a List-items list. The balance is the whole justification.

⛔ COLOURING THE MONEY. Red debits and green credits are the reflex and they are not this system's rule. See $moneyColour: the coloured seats exist, are MONO ONLY, and their use on a ledger is unruled and Dave's.
Relying on the status DOT to convey state. The dot is 1.98:1 / 2.18:1 standalone (measured #204); the word is the carrier.

Letting the payee be the element that gives way. A status chip must never crush the merchant name to 'Brist…' — the line wraps and the name claims a basis instead (a defect found by looking at the render at #209).
Re-sorting the rows client-side while showing a running balance. The balance is only true in one order.

$differsFrom.List-items (type=transaction): GATED, PROMOTED, 9.0/9. Its row IS a <button>: one target, one action, independent rows, no column headers and no cross-row relation. It answers 'what was this payment?'. This answers 'what was the balance after it?' — which only exists because of the rows above. Drop the running balance and this component collapses into it.
$differsFrom.Table: Table is the generic data-grid family with no domain. This is a table with exactly one anatomy — money out, money in, balance — and one rule: order is meaning.
$differsFrom.Document-row: Same lane, different subject: that row hands the user a FILE, this row states an AMOUNT and a BALANCE. Document-row's two-action shape is not used here, because a ledger line has no discrete second action.
$differsFrom.Amount-display: The atom whose money FORMAT this composes (symbol before, no space, tabular lining, U+2212). ⚠ amount-display.meta.json's relationships.livesInside already carries 'Transaction / ledger row (gap)' — #204 Lane N's finding 3 explains it: the GATED transaction row contradicts copy-025 and does not compose the atom. This file composes it correctly. IT DOES NOT REPAIR THE GATED ROW; that repair is owed in List-items and is named in the receipt.

$decisionsForDave: ⛔ FIRST: should this exist at all, given #204 ruled row 91 a duplicate? The ledger form is the only part of row 91 that List-items does not hold. If the product's statement is a list, delete this.
Two money columns or one signed column? Both are drawn.
Do ledger CREDITS take the ruled green seat (rag.success-ink, MONO ONLY), or stay monochrome as drawn? Deliberately not taken.
Does a pending row show an em dash where the balance will be, or nothing, or a projected figure?
Is the day-group heading right, or does every row carry its own date column?
The status vocabulary — Pending / Reversed, and settled rows silent. Right set?
What belongs on the reference line, if anything?
Should a ledger line be openable (a receipt view)? That makes the row interactive and re-opens the List-items question.
